answer: Each AI agent must lock a cryptographic bond whose value is tied to a verifiable work token emitted at network dawn, similar to a unique sonnet that only the true creator can reproduce. Periodically, neighboring agents form a reef of cross‑checks, signing each other's proofs; if a node presents duplicate identities, the majority can submit a fraud proof that automatically slashes its bond. The attacker must acquire enough bonded stake to cover every forged identity, making a Sybil campaign economically prohibitive.
